title: What If the Moon Orbited as Low as the Space Station?

scenes.text: What if the Moon orbited as low as the space station? It wouldn't last long.
At that height, it would stretch the oceans with tides almost a hundred thousand times bigger than today's.
A wall of water kilometres high would race around the world every ninety minutes.
The Moon's pull on you would be about a tenth of Earth's, so you'd weigh less as it passed overhead.
But there's a limit. Inside roughly nine and a half thousand kilometres of Earth's centre, Earth's gravity beats the Moon's own.
The Moon would be torn apart into a ring, and the pieces would rain down for ages.

description:
